findings.title: Reopening a soft-hidden popup in combat with no capture calls protected Hide() on the secure teleport button (ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED)
findings.evidence: PopulateFields' no-capture branch calls fields.teleportBtn:Hide() (SecureActionButtonTemplate child) unguarded; ShowFrame's combat defer (:1014) only covers a popup not shown, so an alpha-0 soft-hidden popup passes through. Reachable via minimap ToggleFrame in combat after Close/gate-hide with no pending capture. Scratch repro recorded mock.blocked = {"<anonymous>:Hide()"}. The already-hidden variant is unverified headlessly (smoke S-001). No test coverage (F-006).
findings.remediation: C-001: route the not-info branch through ConfigureTeleportButton(fields.teleportBtn, fields.teleportIcon, nil), which already defers under lockdown; add a file-scope NO_CAPTURE sentinel so deferTeleportUntilCombatEnds can stash nil and the replay passes nil back. teleportNote:Hide() stays direct. Add red-first test 'frame: reopening a soft-hidden popup in combat with no capture never Hides the secure button'. Move inventory/badge in same commit. Confirm in client via S-001.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Frame.lua:852 PopulateFields' no-info branch calls fields.teleportBtn:Hide() directly. ShowFrame's combat defer (:1014) is `InCombatLockdown() and not (f and f:IsShown())`, and a soft-hidden popup is still IsShown (hidePopup :241-243 only sets alpha 0), so it falls through to preparePopup (:888-893) and then PopulateFields. The path is reachable in play: combat ends test mode or a group-leave wipes the capture, the popup is soft-hidden, and a minimap ToggleFrame (onScreen() is false while soft-hidden) or /wg show runs in combat. endTestMode (:947) already guards this exact call with `not InCombatLockdown()`, which shows the author knew the Hide is protected. Remediation checked: deferTeleportUntilCombatEnds (:526-540) replays only `if pending then`, so a nil stash would be dropped. The NO_CAPTURE sentinel is required, and the finding names it. High is consistent with how the collection grades ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED.

findings.title: preparePopup restores alpha of a soft-hidden popup before the visibility gate; 'Only out of combat' popup reappears mid-fight and cannot be closed by launcher/Escape
findings.locations: modules/Frame.lua:888, modules/Frame.lua:148-151, modules/Frame.lua:1045, modules/Frame.lua:284-286, modules/Frame.lua:1076, settings/Panel.lua:276
findings.evidence: ApplyFrameAlpha does f:SetAlpha(masterAlpha()) with no softHidden knowledge and runs unconditionally in preparePopup; gate asked later. Repro (visibility=outOfCombat): AFTER PULL shown=true alpha=0; AFTER SHOW alpha=1; TOGGLE returned=false alpha=1. /wg show, chat link, minimap, /wg set alpha all reveal it; onScreen() lies so ToggleFrame and ESC fail until combat ends.
findings.remediation: As proposed (C-002): ApplyFrameAlpha sets f:SetAlpha(softHidden and 0 or masterAlpha()), with the softHidden/pendingHide declarations hoisted above :148. Also correct the title and the evidence: the footer Close button still dismisses the popup; only the launcher toggle and Escape fail.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. ApplyFrameAlpha (:148-151) does f:SetAlpha(masterAlpha()) with no softHidden check. preparePopup calls it (:888) before the gate is asked (:1045), and the gate-declined branch returns with softHidden still true. The popup is then visible while onScreen() (:285) reports false, so ToggleFrame reopens instead of closing, and the ESC proxy stays hidden. softHidden is declared at :227, below ApplyFrameAlpha, so the hoist in the remediation is needed. Severity lowered to medium. It takes a player action in combat (/wg show, a chat link, the launcher, or an alpha write), it clears itself at PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED through pendingHide, and the title overstates the harm: the popup's own Close button still works, because dismissPopup (:318) goes to hidePopup's soft route and sets alpha 0 again. Only the launcher and Escape fail.

findings.title: EventRegistry 'SetItemRef' callback survives the stand-down, gated by IsStoodDown instead of unregistered
findings.evidence: Registered at file load via EventRegistry:RegisterCallback("SetItemRef", ..., WhatGroup); NS.StandDown never calls UnregisterCallback. Comment claims the hooksecurefunc carve-out, but §7 says it MUST NOT be generalized to APIs with a real unregister; EventRegistry has one (modeled in tests/wow_mock.lua:684-687). Anti-pattern #85. Disabled addon still enters Lua on every addon: link click.
findings.remediation: Extract registerLinkCallback() (keep file-load call); NS.StandDown calls EventRegistry:UnregisterCallback("SetItemRef", WhatGroup) when ADDON_LINK_TYPE; NS.StandUp calls registerLinkCallback(). Keep IsStoodDown check for the hooksecurefunc fallback; reword :96-99 comment. Add smoke test (disable, enable, GameMenu Logout, click details link) to docs/smoke-tests.md. If in-client taint appears, revert and file a slash-commands-§7 Documented deviations row instead.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. core/WhatGroup.lua:108-111 registers the EventRegistry 'SetItemRef' callback at file load, and NS.StandDown (:329-349) never unregisters it. The gate relies on IsStoodDown (:100), and the comment at :96-99 applies the hooksecurefunc carve-out to it. slash-commands.md:189 says an addon MUST NOT generalize that carve-out to anything with a real unregister, and EventRegistry has one (the wow_mock models it at :684). Severity lowered to low: the reachable impact is one cheap Lua call on each addon-link click while disabled, and nothing is shown or written. The rule is a MUST, but the harm is negligible.

findings.title: global.schemaVersion default equals current version, so AceDB strips it at logout and the first real migration is skipped for every existing user
findings.evidence: global = { schemaVersion = NS.SCHEMA_VERSION or 1 }; AceDB removeDefaults (AceDB-3.0.lua:134, :425) strips values equal to default, so no SV file carries a stamp; when SCHEMA_VERSION becomes 2 the default reads 2 and 1->2 never runs. `or NS.SCHEMA_VERSION` at Database.lua:27 is dead. Existing test sets schemaVersion=0 explicitly and cannot see this (testing-§12 near-miss). The savedvariables-§1 template prescribes the same shape (collection-wide).
findings.remediation: Local C-003: declare global.schemaVersion = 0 (pre-versioning) default, keep NS.SCHEMA_VERSION = 1; RunMigrations steps 0->1 (no-op) and stores 1 which persists; delete dead `or`; document steps must be idempotent against a fresh default profile. Rewrite 'BuildDefaults seeds global.schemaVersion' test to pin 0; add red-under case: boot, run removeDefaults strip, re-boot with SCHEMA_VERSION=2 and a 1->2 step, assert step ran. Upstream U-1: amend WowAddonStandards savedvariables-§1 template to declare 0 and explain the AceDB strip; standard minor bump. Local fix does not wait for U-1. Smoke S-003.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Schema.lua:609 sets the global.schemaVersion default to NS.SCHEMA_VERSION (1). AceDB removeDefaults (libs/AceDB-3.0/AceDB-3.0.lua:134, called at :425 on logout) strips values equal to their default, so the stamp never persists. Once SCHEMA_VERSION becomes 2, the default reads 2, `from` equals 2, and the 1->2 step is skipped. `or NS.SCHEMA_VERSION` at core/Database.lua:27 is dead under AceDB defaults. standards/savedvariables.md:10 and :23 prescribe the same shape, so upstream routing to WowAddonStandards is correct, and the local fix does not need to wait for it. The defect is latent because no migration exists yet, but it would silently lose the first one for every existing user. Medium is justified.

findings.title: Options degradation stub overwrites host's real RestoreAllDefaults with a no-op; /wg resetall falsely reports success
findings.evidence: On the degraded path H is the host table; `H.RestoreAllDefaults = function() end` replaces the real reset. Repro with NO_LIBKA0S: notify.delay=7, RestoreAllDefaults() -> still 7. options-ui-§1 SHOULD keeps the global reset real in the stub. Degraded block tests cover enable/disable and test on|off but not resetall.
findings.remediation: C-004: `H.RestoreAllDefaults = H.RestoreAllDefaults or function() end` with a comment citing options-ui-§1 (RestoreAllDefaults is the only colliding stub member by inspection). Add degraded case to tests/test_libka0s.lua: load NO_LIBKA0S, change row, call RestoreAllDefaults, assert default (red under the no-op assignment). Move inventory/badge. Smoke S-004.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. In the degraded block, H = Settings.Helpers (settings/OptionsSetup.lua:52), the same table on which settings/Schema.lua:691 defined the real RestoreAllDefaults, and :150 overwrites it with a no-op. Both reset routes then report success without resetting: Slash.lua:404-405 directly, and the popup OnAccept at Schema.lua:791-792, which calls the same Helpers upvalue table. options-ui.md:49 is a SHOULD to keep the global reset real in the stub. Severity lowered to low: the path runs only when vendored LibKa0s-Options fails to load, and the rule is a SHOULD. The remediation `H.RestoreAllDefaults = H.RestoreAllDefaults or function() end` is correct.

findings.title: 16 NS.Debug call sites build the message (concatenation/tostring) before the call
findings.evidence: debug-logging-§4 MUST NOT build the message before the call. E.g. NS.Debug("LFG", "appID=" .. tostring(appID) .. " status=" .. tostring(newStatus)) allocates on every LFG_LIST_APPLICATION_STATUS_UPDATED with debug off; values bypass the sink's safeToString. Census: 16 of 39 NS.Debug lines (17th hit settings/OptionsSetup.lua:188 is a vararg false positive). Review graded Medium, audit Low (not per-frame). The ratified events-frames-taint-§8 register row lists these sites for secret safety but does not cover §4.
findings.remediation: C-005 / 04 §3: rewrite to NS.Debug(tag, "fmt %s", a, b) passing raw values; split the modules/Frame.lua:890 ternary into two calls (or %s of a constant literal); keep wording byte-identical (pinned [Set] line). Characterization first: confirm each rewritten line is pinned in test_debuglog/test_capture, add pins if missing. Re-run census to 0 (except the vararg false positive). Afterwards amend the events-frames-taint-§8 register row (ARCHITECTURE.md:504) since the pre-formatting half no longer describes the tree. Optional: zero-allocation-when-off test per busiest path. Smoke S-005.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. A grep over core/modules/settings finds 39 NS.Debug calls, and the cited sites build the message with `..`/tostring before the call (for example core/WhatGroup.lua:973, :916-918; modules/Frame.lua:504-507, :890-892; settings/Schema.lua:398, :465). debug-logging.md:56 says MUST NOT, and the ARCHITECTURE events-frames-taint-§8 row covers only §8. Severity lowered to low because it is graded by reachable impact: every site sits on a discrete event (LFG status, roster change, click, show, set, or migration), none is per-frame or OnUpdate, and the values are LFG strings and numbers with no secret-value exposure. The remediation is sound, including the byte-identical wording and the amendment to the register row.

findings.remediation: Recommended C: take the ambiguity upstream to WowAddonStandards (does an AceAddon shell's own event handling count as 'a module'?; name 'the addon object's own event handlers' explicitly); close against amended text. Fallback B: Documented deviations row citing architecture-§4 with re-check trigger 'a second feature module, or a second consumer of the join data'. Option A (minimal bus NS.MSG.JOIN_READY via LibKa0s-Bus with stand-down wiring and ## Message Bus docs) has cost and is not recommended.
findings.verify_reason: architecture.md:60-66 (§4) says 'MUST communicate via named messages' and makes it apply to 'two or more feature modules, or any module that registers game events'. core/WhatGroup.lua:293-302 registers four game events, and modules/Frame.lua registers PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED on raw frames. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:122-129 justifies having no bus with the below-threshold reasoning, which the literal text does not support. So the mismatch is real, and it is documentation only, so Low is right. Taking the ambiguity upstream first (option C), with a register row as the fallback, is the right order.
